drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Let's start with an item. A retail bank wants Claude to handle card dispute emails: read the message
drills.answer_line: SAM: B, and every piece maps to this episode.
drills.stem: A bank's agent handles card dispute emails: decide provisional-credit eligibility under the bank's published rule, look up the transaction in core banking, draft a reply. Pilot traces show every email followed one of three paths. Which change best fits the requirements?

options.A: Keep the agent and add a logging tool that records each eligibility decision for audit
options.B: Routing workflow: Claude extracts and drafts, rules engine decides, tool fetches, human approves big credits
options.C: Move the agent to Opus with extended thinking so eligibility judgments improve
options.D: Index the transaction history in a vector store so the agent needs fewer tool calls

drills.why: Three observed paths rule out an agent. The published rule stays in the rules engine, live transactions need a tool call, and a human approves larger credits.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A field-service company extracts part numbers, fault codes and dates
drills.answer_line: ALEX: B. Format is a valid trigger, but only after prompting has failed
drills.stem: A field-service company extracts part numbers, fault codes and dates from technician notes. Formats vary run to run and downstream parsing breaks. Volume is moderate, latency not critical. An engineer proposes fine-tuning, since consistent format is an accepted reason. Best next step?

options.B: Add an output contract, then structured outputs or evaluator-optimizer; fine-tune only if format still fails
options.C: Convert the extraction into an agent that retries until parsing succeeds

drills.why: Format is a valid fine-tuning trigger only after prompting has failed, and nobody has tried a proper output contract.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A hospital network reviews a patient's records before
drills.answer_line: ALEX: A and B. A catches the count gap, B recovers at the boundary
drills.stem: A hospital network reviews a patient's records before a procedure, one subagent per document. The report reads "38 documents reviewed, no contraindications found". The file held 40. Which two changes address the root cause?

options.A: A synthesis rule that results returned must equal documents dispatched, flagging any shortfall
options.B: Retry failed or empty subagent results, recording any that still fail as gaps
options.C: Upgrade the orchestrator to the most capable model
options.D: Have the orchestrator re-read every document itself
options.E: A dashboard of average subagent latency

drills.why: A catches the count gap at synthesis; B recovers at the subagent boundary, where recovery is possible. A smarter orchestrator still counts only what came back.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A government agency gets tens of thousands of consultation responses
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Nearly said productivity. But reading everything wasn't possible before
drills.stem: A government agency gets tens of thousands of consultation responses. Staff read a 10% sample because reading all is impossible. With Claude themeing every response and analysts reviewing the themes, every response is now considered. Which pillar does this primarily advance?
drills.why: Reading every response was not possible before, so it is transformation. Efficiency is the same sample faster; productivity is more of work the team could already do.
